content.user_title: Block Risky Git Commands in Claude Code
content.value_statement: AI coding sessions can accidentally run destructive git commands. This skill installs a Claude Code hook that stops high-risk git operations before execution.
actual_capabilities: Guides installation of a Claude Code PreToolUse hook for Bash commands.
Blocks git push, reset --hard, clean, branch deletion, checkout dot, and restore dot patterns.
Includes a test command to verify that dangerous git commands are blocked.
limitations: Requires Claude Code hook support and a shell environment that can run the bundled script.
Requires jq for parsing Claude Code hook input.
Uses pattern matching, so custom git aliases or unusual command forms may need extra rules.
Does not replace normal git review, branch protection, or repository permissions.

use_cases.title: Protect personal projects from accidental git pushes
use_cases.description: Install project-level guardrails so Claude Code cannot push, hard reset, or clean files without user intervention.
use_cases.target_user: Solo developers using Claude Code in local repositories

use_cases.title: Standardize AI coding safety for a team
use_cases.description: Share a repeatable hook setup that blocks destructive git commands during assisted development sessions.
use_cases.target_user: Engineering leads and developer experience teams

use_cases.title: Add global safety defaults for frequent AI coding
use_cases.description: Configure a global Claude Code hook when a user wants the same git protections across all projects.
use_cases.target_user: Power users who work across many repositories

prompt_templates.prompt: Install the git guardrails globally for Claude Code. Preserve any existing settings and verify that git push is blocked.

output_examples.input: Set up git guardrails for this project only.
output_examples.output: The assistant asks for confirmation, copies the hook into the project .claude directory, updates project settings, and verifies that git push is blocked.

output_examples.input: Add protection against git reset --hard and git clean -fd.
output_examples.output: The assistant confirms the denylist includes both commands and tests the hook with safe sample input.

output_examples.input: Install this for all my Claude Code projects.
output_examples.output: The assistant explains the global scope, updates the user Claude settings after approval, and keeps existing hook entries intact.

best_practices: Choose project scope unless you intentionally want the same rule across every repository.
Keep existing Claude Code hooks when adding this configuration.
Run the verification test after installation and after changing blocked patterns.
anti_patterns: Do not overwrite an existing settings file when adding the hook.
Do not assume this hook replaces branch protection or code review.
Do not add broad patterns without testing legitimate git workflows.

faq.question: What does this skill block?
faq.answer: It blocks common destructive git commands, including push, reset --hard, clean, branch deletion, checkout dot, and restore dot.

faq.question: Does it run git commands itself?
faq.answer: No. The hook reads the command Claude Code planned to run and blocks matching dangerous patterns.

faq.question: Can I install it for only one project?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill supports project-level installation through the project .claude settings file.

faq.question: Can I install it globally?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill also supports global installation through the user Claude settings file after the user chooses that scope.

faq.question: Can I change the blocked commands?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill asks whether you want to add or remove patterns after copying the hook script.

faq.question: What dependency does the hook need?
faq.answer: The script uses jq to parse Claude Code hook input, so jq must be available in the shell environment.
